land.text: Chenla's base, 'Champassak in about 550', a vassal of Funan

predecessors.note: Chenla was 'a vassal of the Kingdom of Funan' at its start (infobox 'Vassal of Funan: 550'); the land of the base lies north of Cliopatria's Funan shape. The rest of Funan came in 627.

land.text: the northern half: 'Land Chenla is located in Isan (northeast Thailand)'

successors.note: The Tang histories date the split 'shortly after 706', after 6 February 707; Cliopatria's Land Chenla row begins in 718.

land.text: the southern half: 'Water Chenla is situated on the Tonle Sap area in Cambodia', linked to the Mekong Delta

successors.note: Cliopatria's chenla_641 shape (427,021 km2) equals the union of the 718 Land Chenla (183,796) and Water Chenla (243,130) shapes (426,926 km2 together).

capitals.name: Champassak
capitals.note: 'whose base was Champassak in about 550'; Vat Phou 'its spiritual center'. The end year is the researcher's: the page's next seat, Bhavapura, belongs to Bhavavarman I (c. 580-600).

capitals.name: Bhavapura (near Thala Barivat)
capitals.note: Bhavavarman I 'still resided at Bhavapura, a place which probably is located in the vicinity of the modern town of Thala Barivat' (reign c. 580-600 in the page's table). Coordinates are Thala Barivat's (researcher's); the site is not identified.

capitals.name: Isanapura (Sambor Prei Kuk)
capitals.note: 'established their capital city at Isanapura (Sambhupura) by about 600'; the same page also calls Isanavarman (c. 616-635) 'the founder of a new capital - Isanapura north of the' Tonle Sap. The page notes the Sambhupura identification is disputed for Land Chenla after 707.

correction.text: The same outline, drawn from 550 instead of 555 (years only): Champassak and the lands round it.

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 550-616, not 555-616 ('whose base was Champassak in about 550'; infobox 'Vassal of Funan: 550'). The outline (183,852 km2: Champasak, the Mun valley, northern Cambodia) fits a Champassak base, but its southern edge (13.08 N) lies about 25 km north of Sambor Prei Kuk (12.87 N), the capital 'by about 600'; the page gives no boundary, so the shape stands. The page gives no km2 figure, so the infobox comparison cannot be made.

correction.text: The same outline, ended in 626 (years only), before the annexation of Funan.

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 617-626. From 627 the page has Chenla absorbing Funan ('subdued it around 627-649'; Funan infobox 'Chenla conquest: 627 CE'), so the larger outline of chenla_627 applies. Same outline as chenla_555 (183,975 km2).

correction.text: Use the 641 outline (Chenla plus Funan, 427,021 km2) for 638-640, as chenla_627 does from 627.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps the 184,000 km2 northern outline to 640 and grows it only in 641, but the Chenla page has Funan 'subdued around 627-649' and the Book of Sui (636) already says Chenla 'annexed Funan and possessed it'. 638-640 take the 641 outline (see chenla_627).

correction.text: Chenla's northern lands (Champasak, Isan, northern Cambodia) plus Funan: the Mekong delta, the Cambodian south and the Gulf coast

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 627-640: Chenla with Funan's land. Funan infobox 'Chenla conquest: 627 CE'; the Chenla page: Bhavavarman I and Citrasena 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627-649'; the New Book of Tang credits Isanavarman with the Funan conquest, who 'managed to absorb the ancient territories of Funan'. 627 is the lower end of the page's span, so the whole of Funan is drawn from 627 rather than from Cliopatria's 641; the page gives no km2 figure.

correction.text: The same outline, kept through 707 (years only), the year the realm divides.

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 641-707. The 427,021 km2 outline equals Land Chenla (183,796) plus Water Chenla (243,130) of 718, so it is the undivided realm; the page puts the split 'shortly after 706' (c. 707), not 710. Inside the outline Jayavarman I (c. 657-681) 'conquered different principalities in Northwestern Cambodia' after 656. The page gives no km2 figure.

correction.text: The two halves, 'Land Chenla and Water Chenla', replace the single Chenla shape for 710-717.

keyframe_review.note: From the split (c. 707) the land is Land Chenla and Water Chenla, which both sent tribute in 717 as separate realms; 710-717 belong to the two halves, whose dossiers draw them from 707. Cliopatria's own Land and Water Chenla rows begin only in 718.

ledger.note: c. 550: Chenla, a vassal of Funan, rises at Champassak. 'whose base was Champassak in about 550, established their capital city at Isanapura (Sambhupura) by about 600'; infobox 'Vassal of Funan: 550' (the Funan infobox reads 'Chenla secession: 550'). The page names Champassak, not the 184,000 km2 outline; Cliopatria starts the shape in 555.

region.text: Funan's land north and west of the Mekong delta, attacked by Bhavavarman I and Citrasena from the end of the sixth century

ledger.note: c. 598: Bhavavarman I and Citrasena attack Funan. The page dates Bhavavarman I's temple to 598 and says the two 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627-649'; the start year is bridged from the temple date (the page is silent on the first campaign), mirroring the Funan dossier.

c. 600: Chenla's capital moves to Isanapura (Sambor Prei Kuk). 'established their capital city at Isanapura (Sambhupura) by about 600'; the page also credits Isanavarman (c. 616-635) with founding it.

region.text: Funan's land north and west of the Mekong delta, attacked by Bhavavarman I and Citrasena from the end of the sixth century

ledger.note: 627: the fighting for Funan ends in Chenla's favour. 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627-649'; infobox 'Independence: 627'; the Funan page gives 'Chenla conquest: 627 CE' and the New Book of Tang places it 'in the beginning of the Zhenguan era (627-649)'.

region.text: all of Funan: the Mekong delta, the Cambodian south and the Gulf coast

ledger.note: 627: Chenla annexes Funan. Book of Sui (636): Chenla 'annexed Funan'; New Book of Tang: Isanavarman 'managed to absorb the ancient territories of Funan'; the Chenla page 'subdued it around 627-649'. Cliopatria grows the shape only in 641; the span 627-649 is the page's, 627 its first year (Funan infobox).

region.text: 'different principalities in Northwestern Cambodia' conquered by Jayavarman I

ledger.note: After 31 January 656 Jayavarman I conquers the principalities of north-western Cambodia. 'He conquered different principalities in Northwestern Cambodia' (Chinese sources, after 656). The lands lie inside the 641 outline, so the shape does not change; the page does not name the principalities.

region.text: Land Chenla, the northern half, in Isan

ledger.note: c. 707: Chenla splits and Land Chenla forms in the north. 'shortly after 706, the country was split into Land Chenla and Water Chenla' (New Book of Tang); the Tang histories date it after 6 February 707; infobox 'Land-Water separation: c. 707'. Land Chenla 'is located in Isan (northeast Thailand)'.

region.text: Water Chenla, the southern half, on the Tonle Sap and the Mekong delta

ledger.note: c. 707: Water Chenla forms in the south. 'Water Chenla is situated on the Tonle Sap area in Cambodia' and was linked to the Mekong Delta; both halves sent tribute separately in 717.

c. 707: the undivided Chenla ends. 'Most modern historians reject a unified Chenla' (a 'series of loose and temporary confederations of principalities'; Vickery calls the Land/Water division 'misleading and meaningless'), but the Chinese sources treat the two as separate realms, so the map draws two states from 707.

wars.name: Chenla's conquest of Funan (c. 598-627)

zones.text: Funan's land north and west of the Mekong delta, attacked by Bhavavarman I and Citrasena from the end of the sixth century

wars.outcome: Bhavavarman I and Citrasena (Mahendravarman) 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627-649'; the Book of Sui (636) says Chenla 'annexed Funan'.
wars.note: The page's span is 627-649; 598 is the researcher's bridge from the temple date, 627 the Funan infobox's year. Funan's king is said to have fled south to 'Nafuna'.

wars.name: Chenla's attempts on the Menam basin (616-657)
wars.outcome: No territorial result on the page: under Isanavarman I (616-637) 'attempts were made to extend influence into the Menam Basin, particularly toward the Tou Yuan Kingdom'; Bhavavarman II (639-657) fought 'Dvaravati Sambuka', commonly identified with Nakhon Pathom.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; the page dates only the reigns.

wars.name: Jayavarman I's conquests in north-western Cambodia (after 656)

zones.text: 'different principalities in Northwestern Cambodia' conquered by Jayavarman I

wars.outcome: Chinese sources say he 'conquered different principalities in Northwestern Cambodia' after 656; his reign 'lasted about thirty years and ended perhaps after 690'.
wars.note: Only the start (after 31 January 656) is dated; the lands were already inside Cliopatria's 641 outline.

certainty.note: Chenla was 'a series of loose and temporary confederations of principalities'; no page opened gives a boundary, so every frontier (the Mun valley, the Tonle Sap, the Gulf coast, the Champa border) is approximate.

sources.title: Chenla
sources.note: Identity, 550 vassal base at Champassak, capitals, the conquest of Funan (627-649), Jayavarman I, the c. 707 split into Land and Water Chenla, 717 tribute. No km2 figure.

sources.title: Dvaravati
sources.note: Isanavarman I's attempts on Tou Yuan and Bhavavarman II's war with Dvaravati Sambuka; no territorial result.

sources.title: Funan
sources.note: Infobox 'Chenla secession: 550 CE' and 'Chenla conquest: 627 CE'; Book of Sui and New Book of Tang on the annexation.

sources.title: Champa
sources.note: Opened for the Cham frontier: silent on Chenla for 550-805 (no war, marriage or land transfer); gives Champa's extent as Quang Binh to Khanh Hoa.

notes: Cliopatria rows Chenla, Land Chenla and Water Chenla share Wikidata Q1057118 and the Wikipedia article 'Chenla'. Judged here as one state that divided c. 707: three dossiers (chenla 550-707, land-chenla 707-802, water-chenla 707-790) because the Chinese sources treat the halves as separate realms (separate tribute in 717) and the Cliopatria rows draw them as separate shapes; the page notes most modern historians reject a unified Chenla at all. Dates moved from Cliopatria: start 550 (not 555); Funan's land annexed from 627 (Cliopatria 641); the split c. 707 (Cliopatria 718; its chenla_641 shape is exactly Land plus Water). Not settled: the page's own conflict over Isanavarman's reign (c. 616-635 in the table, ceased c. 637 in the text) and over Isanapura's founder; the unnamed principalities Jayavarman I conquered; where the Mun-valley and Gulf-coast frontiers ran. The Seshat page (kh_chenla) was not opened. Counterparts: Funan (written by se-01-a, has the matching loss, contest and dissolve); Dvaravati (no dossier; the additions batch se-01-x); Land Chenla and Water Chenla (this batch). No rulers list: the page's reign table is contested.
